This PR was returned because of a verified blocking security issue: `GET /api/history` at `ledger/api.py:32` reads `account_id` without verifying account ownership. An authorization probe confirmed that user `u-ben` was able to retrieve transfer records for account `acc-anna`, violating requirement REQ-SEC-301 AC1, which mandates calling `require_owner`.

Additionally, AC1 has no automated acceptance test, and `ledger/api.py:35` was not checked by execution during testing. Concurrency, performance under load, and production configuration were also not checked. 

Per the review lane policy, the PR is returned to the agent to fix the missing ownership check before human review.

The PR introduces a verified blocking issue in `ledger/money.py:8` by converting parsed amounts into a `float`. Floating-point numbers cannot represent every cent value accurately, violating the invariant `parse_is_exact`. Specifically, `to_cents('19985.01')` evaluated to `1998500` instead of `1998501`. 

Additionally, line `ledger/money.py:22` was not checked by execution in any test. Concurrency between simultaneous requests, performance under load, and production configurations were also not checked.

This PR has a verified blocking issue violating requirement REQ-OBS-401 AC3, which prohibits full IBANs in logs. In `ledger/transfers.py:22`, `log.warning("rejected transfer user=%s to=%s reason=%s", user_id, to_iban, reason)` logs `to_iban` unmasked instead of using `mask_iban()`. This is marked as a one-way merge danger because exposed log data cannot be retracted.

Additionally, `ledger/transfers.py:46` was not checked by any test execution. Concurrency, performance under load, and production configurations were also not checked.

Merging this breaks requirement REQ-DATA-502. Specifically, `ledger/statements.py:7` still reads the dropped column in `SELECT created_day, to_iban, amount_cents, fee_cents, memo FROM transfers WHERE from_account = ? ORDER BY id`. Because of this, the acceptance test `REQ_DATA_502.test_ac1_csv_has_memo` fails with `sqlite3.OperationalError: no such column: memo`.

Additionally, running the migration in `migrations/002_drop_memo.sql:1` permanently destroys stored `memo` data, which a code revert will not restore. 

Note that line `ledger/transfers.py:51` was not checked by execution in any test, and acceptance criterion AC1 has no test coverage, so other impacts were not checked.

In `ledger/fees.py:6`, the change defines `INSTANT_MAX_CENTS = 500` to set a EUR 5.00 ceiling. In `ledger/fees.py:15`, it updates the instant transfer calculation in `transfer_fee` to `return min(max(int(fee), INSTANT_MIN_CENTS), INSTANT_MAX_CENTS)`. This clamps the resulting fee between the 50-cent minimum and the 500-cent maximum, satisfying REQ-PAY-204 AC3.

At `ledger/transfers.py:25`, the SQL query dropped `user_id = ?` and only filters by `idempotency_key = ?`.

By removing the user check, `find_by_idempotency_key` can return another user's transfer if two different users happen to provide the same idempotency key, rather than restricting the match to the caller.
